36: - "expected value": selects the asteroid with the highest expected value of all drops when destroyed.
37: - "quality": selects the asteroid with the highest value ore.
38: The strategy that the "Board selected ship" control uses for selecting ships when you have none targeted.
40: - "value": selects the highest value ship, with the value being estimated if you haven't scanned the outfits of the ship.
41: - "mixed": accounts for the value divided by the distance to the ship.
42: The strategy that your escorts use for determining when to fire their secondary weapons. Able to be toggled by the "Fleet: Toggle ammo usage" control.
43: - "never": your escorts will never use their secondary weapons.
44: - "frugal": your escorts will only fire their secondary weapons when their HP is low or the hostiles in the system are stronger than your fleet and friendlies.
45: - "always": your escorts will always use their secondary weapons when firing.
46: Control which of your ships can pick up flotsam (cargo floating in space). Flotsam is picked up automatically when your ships overlap it.
47: - "off": your ships will never pick up flotsam.
48: - "flagship only": only your flagship will pick up flotsam.
49: - "escorts only": only your escorts will pick up flotsam.
50: - "on": your entire fleet will pick up flotsam.
51: The strategy used for repairing carried ships (e.g. fighters, drones) in your fleet while they are docked with their carrier.
52: - "series": repairs the highest HP ship until it is fully repaired, then moves on to the next one.
53: - "parallel": repairs the lowest HP ship at all times so that all ships increase in HP together.
54: When deployed, your fighters and drones will automatically recall themselves to the carrier if their health drops below 50%, then automatically deploy again after healing above 75% if a manual recall command has not been sent.
55: If your fighters cannot be repaired above this threshold while docked in their carrier, they will not leave the carrier if you send another deploy command without holding <shift>.
56: The health of a ship is calculated as its shields plus the amount of hull prior to the ship becoming disabled.
57: Fighters transfer any cargo that they have to their carried ship when they dock.
58: Rehires extra crew whenever you land if you lost additional (non-required) crew while in flight.
59: Automatically unpark a ship dragged to the first position in the ship list, and make it your flagship.
60: When distributing cargo and passengers among your ships on takeoff, prioritize the flagship over your escorts. (When your flagship does not have enough space, some mission cargo or passengers may still be moved to your other ships.)
61: For rush missions, subtract the distance to the destination from the deadline to determine how fast to blink the map marker.
62: Creates a dark shroud over regions of the galaxy that you haven't explored yet. The shroud is lifted as you explore systems.
63: If you have escorts, marks systems with escorts in them on the star map.
64: If you have outfits stored on a planet, marks systems with stored outfits on the star map.
65: Always underline the shortcut key for any buttons. Holding the alt key in any panel will also underline the button shortcut keys if this setting is off. For buttons that contain a character that is underlined twice, the hotkey is shift plus the double underlined character.
67: Disable fast-forward whenever you land or when a conversation, dialog, or other panel appears while in flight.
